record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether SAE reconstruction error can result from sparsity-induced feature suppression and whether decoder fine-tuning without a sparsity penalty reduces it.
record.gate_note: The study reports SAE reconstruction norms, reconstruction MSE, and language-model perplexity after patching reconstructed activations. It does not compare SAE errors with random errors of the same size, examine linear predictability or overlap of error contexts across SAE sizes, test circuit or steering analyses, or isolate dead-latent and architecture effects.
record.test_reason: Tests one training-artifact explanation of SAE error, sparsity-penalty shrinkage ('feature suppression'). It removes the shrinkage after training by fine-tuning decoder or scale parameters without the penalty, then measures how much reconstruction MSE and patched-perplexity gap shrink. This bears directly on V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that the sparsity penalty suppresses features, mostly those with frequent but weak activations. Adding a scale vector and fine-tuning the decoder without the penalty gives about 9% lower MSE and 24% perplexity-gap recovery without changing when features activate. Scale alone gives 6% and 16%. They recommend post-hoc scale fine-tuning when patching SAEs into the model.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines SAE feature suppression and mitigates it by fine-tuning selected SAE parameters without a sparsity penalty; it does not apply the original dark-matter study's error-predictability or cross-size measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Fine-tuning method changes the gains: Decoder, Unrotated Decoder, and Scale differ in their aggregate MSE and perplexity recovery; encoder fine-tuning drastically reduces sparsity.

fits_no_version.finding: Suppression depends on feature activation strength and frequency. Correlation of fine-tuning scaling with log(strength) is -0.710 and with log(frequency) is 0.786.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE shrinkage falls most on frequent, weakly activating features.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning the encoder without the sparsity penalty drastically reduces sparsity (L0 rises).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Encoder-side fixes to reconstruction error trade off against sparsity.

record.problems: Results are limited to Pythia-70m SAEs; no uncertainty estimates are stated. Fine-tuning recovers only part of the reconstruction MSE and perplexity gap. There is no comparison to random errors of the same size, and the study does not establish what fraction of dark matter is explained by suppression.

untested.parts: Other architectures (TopK, JumpReLU, gated), end-to-end training, dead latents (counted but not tested as a cause), and whether gains persist in larger SAEs or models. Only 2048-latent SAEs on Pythia-70m were tested.
Not tested: there is no comparison with random errors of the same norm.

missing.what: Per-layer original and fine-tuned L2 ratios, and dead-feature counts per layer (101-872 of 2048)
Statement that the remaining L2-ratio gap in layers 1-5 may come from missing encoder features that decoder fine-tuning cannot recover
missing.locator: Section 'Fine-tuning Reduces Feature Suppression', Figure 3 text

record.verdict_notes: The post predates the original dark-matter paper. Its result means shrinkage explains a minority of the MSE but a larger share of downstream perplexity harm. The perplexity measure here is the patched-perplexity gap, with original LM perplexity about 38 per the author's comment. It is not a random-error comparison, so it does not bear on V3. The Cunningham et al. 25-to-40 perplexity figure is cited, not a result of this study.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of SAE error is a linear function of the input activation.
Predictability of error norms across SAE sizes, overlap of failed contexts across sizes, and whether error persists with SAE scaling.
The study does not compare the effect of SAE reconstruction errors with random errors of the same size.
Whether linear and nonlinear error components have the stated distinct properties.
Whether circuit or steering analyses lose behavior unless the SAE error term is retained.

The study tests sparsity-induced suppression and decoder fine-tuning, but not better SAE architectures, end-to-end training, or the separate contributions of dead latents and other objective choices; it does not establish what share of all dark matter these effects explain.

relationships.condition: Pythia-70m residual SAEs, decoder or scale fine-tuning without the sparsity penalty
relationships.reason: Shrinkage from the sparsity penalty is real and fixable: L2 ratio rises from about 0.85-0.89 toward 1 (r21, r24). Decoder fine-tuning recovers 24% of the patched-perplexity gap and Scale 16% (r7, r8, r15-r20).
relationships.display_finding: Fine-tuning raised the L2 ratio from about 0.85–0.89 toward 1; decoder and scale fine-tuning recovered 24% and 16% of the patched-perplexity gap, respectively.
